title: Wonderla Holidays Ltd - 538268 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Wonderla Q2 FY27 income rose 42% YoY to INR126 crore and EBITDA 90% to INR30 crore, with Chennai Park driving about 73% of the EBITDA increase.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first full quarter of contribution from Chennai Park, which added about INR28 crore revenue on 1.90 lakh visitors. Existing parks (Bengaluru, Kochi, Hyderabad, Bhubaneswar) grew revenue 8% on 6% footfall growth, and resorts grew 57%. Profit was about INR5 lakh versus a loss a year ago, with PAT held back by a INR10 crore rise in depreciation and higher tax. Management said Chennai will take 2 to 3 years to reach optimal utilisation, and that no new park is yet finalised.

segments.name: Chennai Park
segments.commentary: Q2 footfall 1.90 lakh and revenue about INR28 crore; contributed INR10.37 crore (about 73%) of the Q2 EBITDA increase. H1 footfall 4.32 lakh, revenue about INR73 crore, and INR28.62 crore (58%) of H1 EBITDA growth.

segments.name: Existing parks (Bengaluru, Kochi, Hyderabad, Bhubaneswar)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue +8% YoY on footfall +6% and ARPU +2%; contributed INR1.83 crore (13%) of EBITDA increase. H1 revenue +13%, footfall +7%. Bengaluru Q2 footfall 2.13 lakh (+9%), Kochi 2.02 lakh (+6%), Hyderabad 0.99 lakh (+7%), Bhubaneswar about 20,000 (-20%).

segments.name: Resorts
segments.commentary: Best-ever Q2 with revenue up 57% YoY; contributed INR2.06 crore (14%) of Q2 EBITDA increase and INR4.71 crore (10%) of H1 increase.

guidance_outlook: Chennai Park to take 2 to 3 years to reach optimal utilisation and sustainable profitability; Bengaluru-level footfall in about 3 years, with Phase 2 growth to be assessed by end-FY28.
Management expects Chennai ARPU to remain stable and grow in line with Kochi and Hyderabad over a one-year period; Chennai ATP will stay below Bengaluru.
Margins at existing parks expected to keep expanding over time; quarterly margins likely to be erratic, stabilising after 2 to 3 years.
Management hopes to conclude 2 to 3 new location deals before end-FY27; no final call taken. Next year's capex is not yet committed.
No further equity dilution planned; capex to be funded mainly from internal cash flows, with possible debt later.
Q1 expected to be the strongest quarter for ARPU and Q2 the weakest; Kochi Q3 expected to be good on group business and Christmas season.
capex_capacity: Land cost benchmark: last Chennai land parcel about INR100 crore; a Mumbai-area site could cost close to INR200 crore, per management, which called it speculative.
Management is working on at least one large project in the next 1 to 2 years plus possibly one Tier 2 city; aims for 3 new parks in 3 to 4 years but said 2 may happen.
Large parks cost about INR500 crore-odd; depreciation at about 7-8% of that is charged to P&L, weighing on PAT initially.
Occupancy across parks is about 30% to 40% on a full-year basis; off-season improvement is harder, dependent on weather.
About 40% to 50% of land is still available across parks (less at Hyderabad); resort expansion to other parks to wait for one full year of Bengaluru resort performance.
Captive solar power is in place at all parks; banqueting facilities exist in all parks.
Constraints on new parks cited as government processes and land acquisition; EsselWorld not for sale, management prefers greenfield.
demand_pricing: Q2 ATP down 3% YoY to INR983 because Chennai had a higher share of discounted group visitors; Chennai ATP about INR948, around 10% below Bengaluru.
Non-ticket spend per guest up 11% in Q2 to INR510 and 16% in H1 to INR559; company says non-ticket share is around 30%+ of ARPU, in line with global trends.
Bhubaneswar Q2 decline attributed entirely to weather: heavy rains and cyclones affected about 20 of 30 districts.
Management is pursuing cohort-led pricing and group bookings to lift lean-season and weekday footfall.
Chennai's first monsoon (mid-October to end-November) is being observed; monsoon impact on footfall acknowledged but not yet quantified.
Management declined to comment on Q3 trends to date, saying Chennai has matched Hyderabad and Kochi so far in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Was Chennai's lower Q2 ticket price (about INR948, 20% below the last three quarters' average) a deliberate push for footfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Dheeran Choudhary said the lower price came from a higher mix of discounted group visitors rather than a strategy, and that Chennai ARPU will grow in line with Kochi and Hyderabad over a year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an update on new parks?
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Chittilappilly said there is no update yet and that the team is working on it. Later he said 2 to 3 new locations are being considered, with no final call taken.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Bhubaneswar Q2 decline weather-driven, and how will Chennai handle its first monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Bhubaneswar drop was entirely weather-led, with cyclones affecting about 20 of 30 districts. On Chennai, it said the monsoon will affect footfall but a fuller read needs the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT flat when EBITDA grew 90%, and when will earnings convert better?
qa_highlights.answer: Saji Louiz said the gap is driven by depreciation from large new parks (about 7-8% of roughly INR500 crore investment charged annually), so PAT will soften initially.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add capacity at Bengaluru or extend the resort model to other parks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on Bengaluru capacity additions. Resort expansion elsewhere will wait for one full year of the Bengaluru resort results.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company need equity dilution to fund future parks?
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Chittilappilly said no further equity dilution is planned; internal cash flows can fund most capex, with some debt possible.

risks_watch: Chennai ramp-up is at an early stage: first monsoon season (Q3) and festive-season footfall are unproven, and utilisation may take 2 to 3 years.
Depreciation from new parks is likely to keep PAT growth well behind EBITDA growth.
Pricing mix risk: growing group share is diluting ATP (Q2 ATP -3% YoY), while ARPU growth is only 1% in Q2.
Timing and cost of new park deals remain uncertain: no new site confirmed, land prices volatile, and government and land-acquisition delays cited.
Existing-park footfall is still below earlier peaks at Bengaluru and Kochi, and Bhubaneswar fell 20% in Q2.
Q2 other income of INR9.1 crore (investment gains) makes up a large share of profit, so PAT quality depends on it.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on long-term growth, but noticeably evasive on specifics: new park timelines, capacity additions, Q3 trading and H2 footfall were all deferred. Management also repeatedly said "hard to say" when asked for firm multi-year targets.
key_quotes: We began FY27 on a strong note, and that momentum has been carried on to the second quarter.
Hospitality is becoming increasingly meaningful contributor to our business.
We prefer to do greenfield and more than take over somebody else's asset.
Now we are not looking to do any further equity dilution.
We are looking at 2 to 3 new locations, but no final call has been taken.
